leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used for a genuine shared-state human-agent procurement loop: reading a case, proposing updates, generating a negotiation plan, and adapting to human revision while preserving award authority.
leverage_evidence: Three tools operate on the canonical React sourcing state: get_sourcing_case, update_sourcing_scenario, draft_negotiation_plan.
The workflow explicitly supports BASE CASE -> AGENT PROPOSAL -> HUMAN-REVISED.
execution_rationale: The live workspace loaded and accepted guidance plus a human revision, but the observation did not show a visible changed scenario or confirmation of the revision effect.
execution_evidence: Live observation found the sourcing case, supplier offers, guidance field, and revision controls.
Action succeeded, but after-state exposed no visible confirmation or changed scenario details.
impact_rationale: The concept targets consequential procurement decisions and reduces reconciliation friction while keeping human accountability explicit; broader impact is plausible but not demonstrated with real data.
impact_evidence: Shared procurement decision workspace for supplier offers, constraints, shortlist, and negotiation planning.
Human retains supplier-award authority.
creativity_rationale: The visible human-agent state machine and adaptation to later human edits is a thoughtful application of WebMCP beyond simple UI control.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposal and human revision are first-class states.
Agent must read and adapt to the revised workspace.
s2_notes: Strong concept and live shell; central revision effect was only partially observable.
advance_reason: Distinctive, relevant WebMCP collaboration with a functioning observable entry flow, despite incomplete visible proof of the full loop.

leverage_rationale: The proposed tools expose live dealership inventory, exact vehicle pricing, dealership information, and consent-gated lead submission directly in the dealership page, extending agent assistance through a consequential funnel.
leverage_evidence: Tools include search_inventory, get_vehicle_details, get_dealership_info, submit_lead, and show_search_results.
Lead submission requires explicit consent and validates contact data.
execution_rationale: The assigned live site was blocked by a Cloudflare security verification page, so the claimed inventory and lead workflow could not be verified in the live observation.
execution_evidence: Observation reported dealership site unreachable for meaningful use.
Cloudflare security challenge remained displayed.
impact_rationale: Agent-native inventory search and safe lead handoff could materially reduce car-buying friction and improve accuracy for high-value purchases, though real operation was not observed.
impact_evidence: Targets current dealership inventory and itemized pricing.
Consent record, validation, deduplication, and rate limiting are described.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a production dealership network and carrying the flow from discovery to CRM lead submission is practical and well scoped, though the interaction pattern is conventional commerce automation.
creativity_evidence: Agent can search and inspect the same current inventory rendered to shoppers.
Agent-card discovery avoids per-dealership browser credentials.
s2_notes: Strong claims and potentially high leverage, but the designated demo was fully blocked during live observation.
advance_reason: Central workflow could not be observed because the assigned demo remained behind a Cloudflare challenge.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to computing answers that are absent from the DOM: accessible routes, clearance checks, disputed updates, closure simulation, and human-gated proposals over a validated spatial graph.
leverage_evidence: Fourteen tools cover route computation, clearance, proposals, disputes, and closure simulation.
Route answers are computed from venue geometry and validated topology rather than scraped page text.
execution_rationale: The live studio loaded a concrete venue floor-plan workspace with route controls, queries, export, and an agent-tools panel. The exact agent-driven route workflow was not fully exercised, and the panel was marked not agent-ready.
execution_evidence: Harbor Arts Centre workspace loaded with rooms and route guidance controls.
Observation confirmed coherent studio state and visible agent-tools panel.
impact_rationale: The product addresses high-stakes accessibility information for blind and low-vision visitors and computes person-specific routes with uncertainty and provenance instead of relying on generic accessibility labels.
impact_evidence: Step-free route and doorway-clearance questions are computed inside a venue.
Human review gates all writes and disputed accessibility claims remain recorded.
creativity_rationale: The combination of spatial reasoning, individualized clearance, explainable failures, disputed claims, closure simulation, and proposal-only writes is unusually deep WebMCP design.
creativity_evidence: No-route results identify the blocking door and width.
Agent proposals pass topology validation and require human decision.
s2_notes: Excellent concept and substantial live studio evidence; agent readiness itself was not active in the observed browser.
advance_reason: High-leverage accessibility workflow with strong originality and a functioning, coherent live studio.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is positioned as an agent interface to an on-device AAC system, complementing switch scanning and real-time communication rather than merely exposing generic page actions.
leverage_evidence: Pitch combines AAC, switch scanning, WebRTC, on-device neural prediction, and browser agents.
The interface is designed around communication output for non-speaking users.
execution_rationale: The live AAC interface accepted a help message and Speak action, producing a transcript entry and repeat control with coherent state, although the agent-specific path was not exercised.
execution_evidence: Message box accepted 'I need help'.
Speak produced 'Your message' and an 'Again' control.
impact_rationale: Fast, reliable communication support for people with severe speech and motor disabilities is a high-impact use case, with direct benefit if the claimed real-time and accessibility properties hold.
impact_evidence: Product is explicitly an augmentative and alternative communication system.
Core communication action worked without login.
creativity_rationale: Combining AAC interaction modalities with WebMCP browser-agent assistance is a meaningful and human-centered application, though the observed flow itself was a conventional speak action.
creativity_evidence: Switch scanning and agent context are integrated into the communication product concept.
Emergency controls and chat/call affordances are present.
s2_notes: Core AAC execution was verified; agent-specific behavior remains less directly evidenced.
advance_reason: High-impact accessibility product with a working core communication flow and credible WebMCP role.

leverage_rationale: The design makes WebMCP part of a permissioned purchase lifecycle: an agent evaluates sources, requests payment, and gains a newly registered premium capability only after policy-compliant human-defined authorization.
leverage_evidence: Demo claims nine initial tools and dynamic registration of query_premium_dataset after verified payment.
Per-purchase cap, session budget, auto-approval threshold, escalation, and receipt ledger are integrated.
execution_rationale: The assigned URL was an x402 stats endpoint that timed out twice and did not expose the SpendMCP workspace or purchase flow.
execution_evidence: Observation could not load the endpoint within browser timeout.
No verifiable after-state was available.
impact_rationale: A bounded payment and permission layer could enable safer agent procurement of premium web capabilities, but adoption and real transaction evidence were not observable.
impact_evidence: Human-defined budgets and approval escalation constrain agent spending.
Receipts and dynamic capability changes make authorization auditable.
creativity_rationale: Making payment alter the agent's registered tool surface is a strong, nontrivial WebMCP interaction model with clear policy semantics.
creativity_evidence: Successful payment dynamically adds query_premium_dataset.
Agent chooses value while human controls economic authority.
s2_notes: Potentially standout design, but the designated live URL was an unavailable stats endpoint rather than an observable demo.
advance_reason: Central purchase-and-permission workflow was not reachable in the assigned live observation.

leverage_rationale: The submission describes useful agent-created equal, custom, and formula-based bill splits over shared group state, but the leverage is a relatively straightforward application of WebMCP tools.
leverage_evidence: Four tools let agents find groups and members and create splits.
Humans review splits and only finished bills can be paid.
execution_rationale: The designated demo URL resolved to a Discord invite, not the split-bill application, so no central workflow was observable.
execution_evidence: Observation found no application workflow at the assigned URL.
The bill-splitting URL appears only in packet text, not as the designated demo.
impact_rationale: Collaborative bill splitting addresses a common coordination problem and could save effort, but impact is moderate and no live execution was verified.
impact_evidence: Supports unequal consumption and repayment tracking.
Human review is retained before payment.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic bill-splitting formulas and human review are sensible, but the concept is familiar and lacks observable evidence of distinctive execution.
creativity_evidence: Equal, custom, and question-based splits are described.
s2_notes: Designated URL mismatch prevented any meaningful runtime verification.
advance_reason: No bill-splitting product was available at the assigned demo URL.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used to expose a shared dual-browser workspace to an external agent, allowing the agent to inspect and act on the same multi-pane browsing context rather than operating an isolated chatbot.
leverage_evidence: Submission claims four workspaces and eleven WebMCP tools.
Human and agent operate on the same two browser panes and saved workspace state.
execution_rationale: The live dual-pane workspace loaded and Capture workspace succeeded with a coherent state, although the observed action did not demonstrate an agent mutation or cross-pane result.
execution_evidence: Left and right panes, separate URLs, saved workspaces, and WebMCP controls were visible.
Capture workspace action succeeded.
impact_rationale: Shared browsing context could reduce context switching for research, comparison, and collaborative work, but the broader value depends on agent operations not observed here.
impact_evidence: Dual-browser workspace is usable by a human and intended for an external agent.
Saved workspaces preserve shared context.
creativity_rationale: Treating a split-browser workspace as an agent-operable shared context is a clear and useful WebMCP framing beyond embedding a chatbot.
creativity_evidence: Agent is intended to understand and interact with panes and workspace controls.
Capture workspace provides an explicit shared-state operation.
s2_notes: Strong live shell and coherent concept; agent-specific actions were not directly exercised.
advance_reason: The central shared-workspace product loaded and performed its capture action, with credible WebMCP leverage.

leverage_rationale: The escape-room mechanics deliberately divide perception and action: humans observe visual cues while the agent reads state and operates mechanisms, making cooperation necessary rather than ornamental.
leverage_evidence: Three rooms require human visual identification plus agent-controlled operations.
Agent cannot open the final door unless its proposal matches the human decision.
execution_rationale: The live escape-room interface loaded, reset successfully, and clearly enforced disabled agent controls pending an agent scan. The full cooperative solve was not executed.
execution_evidence: Mirror Chamber and agent-operation areas were visible.
Reset action succeeded and agent buttons remained disabled until scan.
impact_rationale: As an accessible demonstration of human-agent complementarity it has educational and entertainment value, but impact is narrower than consequential workflow products.
impact_evidence: Requires complementary human visual perception and agent state/action ability.
Three-stage game structure is described.
creativity_rationale: The neither-party-can-escape-alone mechanic is a particularly clear creative expression of WebMCP's complementary capabilities.
creativity_evidence: Human sees flashing symbols/markers; agent handles mechanisms and structural information.
Actions and blocked attempts are recorded.
s2_notes: Coherent live game and explicit capability boundary; no agent scan was available in the observation.
advance_reason: Distinctive cooperative design with a functioning live interface and clear WebMCP role.

leverage_rationale: Temporal WebMCP dynamically exposes only phase-valid migration tools, making workflow state and correctness part of the tool surface rather than relying on model discipline.
leverage_evidence: Tools appear and disappear based on profiling, planning, execution, and source/mapping state.
Deterministic transformations, validation, dry runs, recovery, and verified export are integrated.
execution_rationale: The polished overview loaded and the Start a migration CTA was clickable, but it did not open the advertised studio or import workflow in the observation.
execution_evidence: Overview clearly presented migration purpose and entry points.
After CTA click remained on overview with no studio/file-import state.
impact_rationale: Reliable migration of messy CSV data is broadly useful, and deterministic validation plus formula-injection protection addresses real operational risks; live completion was not shown.
impact_evidence: Workflow covers profiling through verified export.
Claims recovery, violations, and spreadsheet formula-injection protection.
creativity_rationale: Phase-aware tool registration is a sophisticated and well-matched WebMCP solution to preventing invalid agent actions in multi-step data workflows.
creativity_evidence: Website owns workflow correctness by exposing only valid capabilities.
Stale tools disappear when mappings or source state change.
s2_notes: Strong design and polished entry page, but the central migration flow did not open from the observed CTA.
advance_reason: Highly relevant WebMCP architecture with a coherent live product shell, despite incomplete CTA execution.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is tightly matched to a provenance-heavy RFQ review: the agent reads documents and proposes sourced fields, while the human alone verifies, edits, resolves conflicts, sends, and confirms.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools cover document listing/reading, field proposals, conflicts, missing values, review state, and clarification drafting.
Agent and human reducers are separated so agent tools cannot cross the approval boundary.
execution_rationale: The live sample session switched to Live, reported tools and calls, and populated the review workspace with coherent human-review controls and a disabled confirmation gate.
execution_evidence: Play sample session succeeded and reported 6 tools/2 calls.
Review populated with Enter value and Mark not required controls; confirmation remained disabled appropriately.
impact_rationale: Catching conflicts and missing values before manufacturing quotes can prevent costly errors, and source-linked human review is directly relevant to a consequential business workflow.
impact_evidence: Targets quantity, material, dimensions, tolerance, revision, and other RFQ fields.
Human confirmation is blocked until fields are settled and the change log preserves decisions.
creativity_rationale: The design turns provenance, conflict handling, field locks, and dynamic clarification-tool registration into a coherent human-agent review protocol.
creativity_evidence: A later proposal returns FIELD_LOCKED after a human edits a field.
Clarification tool appears when gaps exist; the person edits and sends.
s2_notes: Strongest observed execution in this batch; live sample visibly demonstrated the agent-to-human review boundary.
advance_reason: High-value workflow, distinctive safety boundary, and strong live evidence of the central sample session.

leverage_rationale: The agent is designed as a second in-world player that authors dialogue, navigates by named destinations, and interacts through game-state tools rather than remotely clicking a UI.
leverage_evidence: Submission claims 24 tools for movement, interaction, dialogue, and waiting for player replies.
Agent-authored lines and choices render in the game's dialogue system; admin-like tools were intentionally omitted.
execution_rationale: The title screen and new-game flow worked, reaching character setup, but the observed session stopped before the claimed 3D office and AI coworker interaction appeared.
execution_evidence: NEW GAME succeeded and opened character setup.
Observation did not yet show the office or agent coworker experience.
impact_rationale: The project offers a novel low-cost form of interactive entertainment and a compelling demonstration of agent-native game design, but direct social or economic impact is limited.
impact_evidence: Static bundle requires no AI backend, keys, or per-player AI cost.
Agent participates as a character rather than a remote controller.
creativity_rationale: Making a browser agent a constrained, in-world coworker that writes fresh dialogue and must cooperate with a human player is highly original for WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Dialogue is authored at runtime and rendered in the game's own UI.
Agent cannot control the player's dialogue, camera, or money.
s2_notes: Very creative concept with working game entry; central agent/office loop was not reached in observation.
advance_reason: Distinctive agent-as-player concept and successful game startup justify advancement despite partial execution evidence.

leverage_rationale: The described tool chain maps resume parsing, job matching, and cover-letter drafting into callable page actions while deliberately keeping final application submission human-only.
leverage_evidence: Tools are parseResume, matchJobs, and draftCoverLetter.
No submitApplication tool exists; apply remains a manual UI decision.
execution_rationale: The live site rendered only an unlabeled Choose File control and hosting links; no job portal, parsing, matching, or drafting workflow was observable.
execution_evidence: Purpose was not identifiable from the rendered page.
No safe meaningful action was available and the page remained a minimal upload surface.
impact_rationale: Automating repetitive resume comparison and tailored drafting could save applicants time while preserving application agency, but the deployed product could not be validated.
impact_evidence: Targets resume-to-job matching and specific cover-letter drafting.
Manual application submission preserves user control.
creativity_rationale: The human-only submission boundary is sensible, but resume parsing and job matching through tools are familiar agent-assistance patterns.
creativity_evidence: Blazor/JS interop bridges tool calls into the same backend logic and database.
Native document.modelContext integration was written to address package mismatch.
s2_notes: Submission describes a complete chain, but the live deployment appeared incomplete or failed to render it.
advance_reason: The assigned live demo did not expose any of the claimed central job-application workflow.
